transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Hi, thank you so much for taking the time to see me, Doctor. I really appreciate it. Um... I hope I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill here, or wasting your time. It's probably nothing serious, but... well, I guess what brought me in is that I've been noticing—or rather, my family and colleagues have been pointing out—that I have a really hard time just staying in my chair. 

Like, if we're in a long staff meeting at school, or even just having dinner at home and everyone else is seated... I just keep getting up. I always try to make it look natural, you know? I'll suddenly pop up to refill the coffee pot, or I'll go double-check a handout, or just walk to the back of the room. But the truth is, I do it even when nothing is really urgent at all. I just... I don't know, I just suddenly feel like I need to move, and sitting still feels almost impossible. 

Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of thing you help people with, I just want to make sure I'm in the right place.
Can you describe what you're feeling inside when you have that urge to get up? Is it more like a physical discomfort, nervous energy, or an anxious feeling that you can't quite sit still with?

Oh, goodness, that’s a really good question. Um... I want to make sure I’m giving you the right answer here. 

I wouldn't really say it's an anxious feeling. I'm actually a very positive person, not really the anxious type at all, I promise! And it doesn't hurt or feel uncomfortable, exactly. It's just... well, honestly, I'm not entirely sure how to describe it. I don't really notice a specific feeling inside. It's more just... a sudden thought that I should probably go be productive, you know? Like I just have a little extra pep in my step, but not in a bad or nervous way. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm sorry if I'm not explaining it very well. I just haven't really stopped to think about the inside part of it before. Is that the kind of answer you were looking for, or should I try to think about it a bit more?

Do you find yourself feeling restless or needing to be constantly doing something, even when you're not in a situation where you're expected to sit still, like at home in the evening or when you're trying to relax?

Well, um... I suppose I do keep pretty busy in the evenings. I hope that’s not a bad thing! I just really like to be productive. 

You know, since the house got a bit quieter—my youngest actually left for college, so it's just me—I find that I just... well, I keep going. I’ll tell myself, 'Okay, tonight I’m just going to sit and rest,' but then I end up moving straight from lesson planning to doing a load of laundry, and then maybe heading out to softball practice, or I'll be in the kitchen chopping food for a community event. 

I just sort of bounce from one thing to the next without much of a pause, even on the nights I really, truly promised myself I’d take it easy. I just like being helpful and getting things done, I suppose! Does that... am I answering your question okay? I hope that doesn't make me sound too frantic or anything.
Do you ever find it hard to focus or stay attentive, especially during tasks that require sustained mental effort, like reading or listening to a lecture?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I hope I'm not misunderstanding what you're asking, but I've never really had trouble with that sort of thing. 

Being a teacher, you know, I'm pretty used to reading and focusing on things. I actually really enjoy my work, and I don't mind putting in the effort. I mean, sure, sometimes if a meeting goes on forever, I might get a little distracted, but I think that happens to everyone, right? I certainly don't think it's a big problem for me. I can always get my grading done and keep up with what I need to do. 

I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm struggling with my mind, because my focus is actually pretty good, I promise!
Do you ever find yourself acting on impulse or making decisions quickly without really thinking them through first?

Oh, goodness, no. I really don't think so. I mean, I hope I don't come across as someone who just does things without thinking! 

As a teacher, you know, you really have to plan ahead and be organized. I'm always making lists and thinking about what needs to happen next. I wouldn't say I'm impulsive at all. I mean, maybe sometimes I'll buy a little treat at the grocery store that wasn't on my list, but nothing major, I promise! I always try to make sure I'm making good, sensible choices. 

I really try to be thoughtful about things. Is that... does that sound like what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm understanding you correctly and giving you the right information.
Do you ever find it difficult to pay attention to details, or do you sometimes make careless mistakes, even when you're trying your best to focus?

Oh, um... well, no, I don't think I really struggle with that. I mean, I certainly try my very best to be careful with everything I do. 

Being a teacher, you know, you're looking at so many papers and details all day long. I'm usually the one catching the mistakes! I mean, I suppose everyone misses a comma here or there when they're grading a huge stack of essays, but I wouldn't say I make careless mistakes. I always try to double-check my work because I really want to do a good job for my students. 

I hope that makes sense? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm sloppy or anything like that, because I really do take a lot of pride in being thorough! Am I giving you the right kind of examples?
Looking back, would you say you had similar tendencies to be restless or have trouble sitting still when you were a child, or is this something that started more recently in your life?

Oh, um... well, I suppose if I really look back, I was always a bit... energetic? I hope that doesn't sound bad! I just mean I've always had a lot of spirit. 

My mother, bless her heart, she used to joke that I wore a literal path in the floorboards between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was even ten years old. And, um, I guess my old report cards did usually say something along the lines of me being a bright girl, but maybe that I had a little trouble staying in my seat or waiting my turn. 

But I always meant well, I promise! I just had so much enthusiasm for learning, you know? It wasn't that I was trying to be disruptive or anything like that. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad student, because I always loved school. Is that the kind of thing you were wondering about? I just want to make sure I'm answering you properly.
Can you tell me if these tendencies to move around or stay busy have ever caused any problems for you, like difficulties in relationships, at work, or in other important areas of your life?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say "problems," exactly. I mean, I really try my best to get along with everyone, and I think I'm generally a very well-liked person! 

But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest, there have been a few little hiccups lately. It's just... well, at school meetings, or even at my Wednesday night book club, I sometimes get so eager to contribute or get things moving that I guess I can be a little... much? I've noticed people sighing or sort of losing patience when I can't quite sit still or let a silence just be a silence. 

It breaks my heart, honestly, because I just want to be helpful and connected to everyone. But sometimes I leave those gatherings feeling a bit embarrassed, like I've rubbed people the wrong way without meaning to. I really don't want to be a bother to anyone, you know? I always try to be a good colleague and friend. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound difficult to work with!
Do you find yourself having trouble settling down or feeling restless in a variety of situations, like when you're out with friends, traveling, or even just sitting through a movie or sermon?

Oh, um... well, I suppose... I mean, I really do try my best to be respectful and attentive, especially in places where you're supposed to be quiet. I definitely wouldn't say I'm causing a scene or anything like that! 

But... well, I guess if I'm sitting for a long time, like when I'm at my desk grading a big stack of essays, or even during a church service, I might... sort of... catch myself moving a little bit? Just small things, really! Like, I might be tapping my foot, or clicking my pen, or just shifting my weight in my seat. 

Sometimes I don't even realize I'm doing it until I have to sort of mentally tell myself, "Okay, time to settle down now." I hope that doesn't sound too awful! I really do try to be still, I just... I guess my body likes to stay busy even when my mind is focused. Is that... is that the sort of thing you're asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
